criteria.evidence: Unchanged since round 1. In 727b58e8 RemotePaymentGateway.packs() is untouched, and RemotePaymentGatewayPacksTest only gains the new constructor argument TestCreditsRepository(), with no assertion change.
Unchanged since round 1. purchase() and the listedProductIds guard (RemotePaymentGateway.kt:119) are untouched. RemotePaymentGatewayPurchaseTest changes only its constructor line.

The pending, retry and repost path is unchanged. recorded() (RemotePaymentGateway.kt:209-220) keeps the same generation and wallet.update guard inside synchronized(reposts) and now launches credits.refresh() only after a Completed result, outside the lock. PurchaseSettleV2Test and PurchaseSettleTest change only their constructor lines.

PurchaseGrantRefreshTest.aGrantedPurchaseRefreshesTheLedgerAndAFailedOneDoesNot shows that a 400 rejection triggers no ledger refresh. The device still never grants: in prod, record() only re-reads the server (OfflineFirstCreditsRepository.kt:51).

Restore goes through settle, post and recorded, so a restored grant now also refreshes the ledger (RemotePaymentGateway.kt:218). PurchaseRestorerTest and PurchaseRestorerPacksTest change only their constructor lines.
No change since round 1. unlock() still makes no request (RemotePaymentGateway.kt:134).
No change since round 1. RemoteCreditsLedgerSource is @Singleton and its owner() reads the Firebase uid.

OfflineFirstCreditsRepository is now @Singleton (line 19). The only binding is the @Binds at DataModule.kt:59 in SingletonComponent. A grep finds no other @Provides or @Binds of CreditsRepository on this branch or on #315 and #317. AppViewModel (#315), TailoringRunner (#317), CollectAccountDataUseCase, DeleteAccountUseCase, SignOutCleaner and RemotePaymentGateway therefore all get the same instance. CreditsRepositorySingletonTest injects two fields and would fail without @Singleton, because each field would get a fresh instance with held == null and the balance would be 0.

In prod, record() calls refresh() (line 51). recordingInProdRefreshesFromTheServer would fail with 6 if record() did nothing. A granted purchase refreshes the ledger (RemotePaymentGateway.kt:218), and PurchaseGrantRefreshTest would fail with 0 if that launch were removed. refresh() catches every failure except cancellation and returns (lines 66-67), so a failed refresh keeps the last good snapshot (refreshFailureKeepsValuesAndAccountSwitchDropsLateAnswer). With the singleton, the D53 retry still works: one refreshCancelled flag is shared, so the next observer of either flow re-fetches (cancelledRefreshIsRetriedWhenNextObserved). D56 interaction: in prod, record() writes no run-<runId> row, so the #317 alreadySpent check (TailoringRunner.kt:38 on revamp/278-tailored) never matches in prod. That is the known #322 gap (D58), tracked and not caused by this diff. One latency side effect is in F1.

SignOutCleaner.clear() calls credits.clear() (SignOutCleaner.kt:23), which bumps the generation and nulls held under the lock (lines 77-81). A late answer is dropped by the generation and owner check (line 70), and refresh() drops a snapshot held for another owner before it fetches (line 58), so a live collector falls to 0 even when the next fetch fails. Mutation check by reading: each of the three new tests fails if its guard is removed, and SignOutCleanerTest would fail with 5 without line 23. Clear while a refresh for the new uid is in flight: RemoteSignInGateway.signIn runs cleaner.clear() after firebase.signIn and before saveAccount (RemoteSignInGateway.kt:51-58). A refresh for user B that is in flight then is dropped by the generation check, and #315 AppViewModel refreshes after the account change, so B sees 0 for a moment and nothing leaks. clear() also wipes the Room credit_ledger in prod. Prod never reads that table (the remote branches at lines 39 and 43), so no visible data is lost.

SignOutCleaner and RemotePaymentGateway are prod-source only. The demo binds NoRemoteLedger, so its record() still inserts and its refresh() returns at once (lines 51 and 55). hilt-android-testing and kspTest(hilt-compiler, kotlin-metadata) are test-only configurations in core/data/build.gradle.kts:32-34, following D57. The dependencyGuard baseline files are unchanged in f9c93f5f..727b58e8. pregate flags this only as NEW_DEPENDENCY warnings.
The diff adds no Log, Timber or println call, and no message that contains a token or uid. The purchase token appears only in a test fixture (PurchaseGrantRefreshTest).

At 727b58e8, Static checks, Core unit tests and Feature unit tests pass. App unit tests, Lint, Screenshot tests and Assemble APKs were still running at review time. delivery-gates-pregate fails with ASSERT_REMOVED on RemotePaymentGatewayTest.kt (-7) and TEST_DELETED on unlock-response.json. Both come from lead commit f9c93f5f, which round 1 adjudicated as justified (contract v2 removes the unlock route), and the PR body pregate section discloses them. In 727b58e8 the testProd edits only add the TestCreditsRepository() constructor argument, and no assertion is removed. The PR body Security notes still say 'prod record() is a no-op', which is now stale.

findings.rule: 287-c10 with the #317 cross-lane contract: a tailoring that the server has stored and charged must report success without waiting on an unrelated ledger read
findings.trigger: In prod, record() now awaits a full GET /credits round trip. On revamp/278-tailored, TailoringCreditSpend.forSuccess calls record() after upsertApplication and before it returns, and TailoringRunner (TailoringRunner.kt:42-61) returns Success only after that. Example: the tailoring POST succeeds and the result is stored, then the network stalls (a train tunnel or a captive Wi-Fi). refresh() blocks for up to the OkHttp call timeout of 75 s (TailorMyResumeHttp.kt:36). The user is charged and the result is on disk, but the screen stays on 'Tailoring' until the fetch fails, and the failure is then swallowed at line 67. If the user leaves, the cancellation sets refreshCancelled and propagates through the runner. Before this diff, record() returned at once in prod.
findings.title: In prod, record() blocks the tailoring success on a GET /credits that can take up to the 75 s call timeout
findings.proof: Use OfflineFirstCreditsRepositoryRemoteTest with remote.gate = CompletableDeferred() and never complete it. Launch record(entry(SPEND, -1, 4)), advance the test scheduler and assert the job is complete. It fails at head because record() suspends on fetch(). Fix sketch: launch the refresh on @ApplicationScope from record(), or have the runner fire and forget it.

findings.rule: 287-c10: the shown balance is the latest server balance. A slower, older answer must not overwrite a newer one.
findings.trigger: The publish guard at line 70 checks only the generation and the owner, so two overlapping refreshes in the same generation publish in completion order, not start order. This diff adds two concurrent refresh sources: record() at line 51, and the launch after a purchase grant at RemotePaymentGateway.kt:218. The onStart retry at line 36 and #315 AppViewModel already call refresh(). Example: refreshCancelled is true (D53). The Credits screen subscribes, and the onStart refresh R1 starts on a slow network while the server balance is 1. The user buys the 5-pack, and recorded() launches R2, which returns 6 quickly and publishes 6. R1 then lands with the pre-grant snapshot of balance 1 and passes the guard (same generation, same owner), so the balance and ledger fall back to 1 until some later refresh. The same thing happens with a spend refresh racing an older one.
findings.title: Overlapping same-generation refreshes publish in completion order, so a stale answer can overwrite the post-purchase or post-spend balance
findings.proof: Use a ScriptedRemote whose fetch() takes a per-call gate. Start refresh R1 on gate1 with snapshot 1, then set the snapshot to 6 and run refresh R2 to completion. Complete gate1 with the old snapshot and assert observeBalance().first() == 6. It fails at head (1). Fix sketch: a monotonically increasing request sequence, so that only an answer whose sequence is newer than the last published one is published.
